title: Background Refetching
description: Control background refetching behavior to keep data fresh without disrupting the user experience.

data.text: React Query can automatically refetch data in the background when certain events occur: the window regains focus, the network reconnects, a new component mounts, or a polling interval elapses. These behaviors keep data fresh without any user intervention, but they can also cause unnecessary requests if misconfigured.

terms.definition: Triggers a background refetch when the user switches back to the browser tab. Enabled by default.
Triggers a refetch when the network connection is restored after being lost.
Polls the query at a fixed interval in milliseconds. Requires a query function that returns a promise.
Refetches stale data when a new component mounts and subscribes to the query.

data.text: React Query provides four main triggers for background refetching. Understanding each helps you configure them appropriately for different data types and user flows.

data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[User Event] --> B{Which Trigger?}
    B -->|Tab Focus| C[refetchOnWindowFocus]
    B -->|Network Up| D[refetchOnReconnect]
    B -->|New Mount| E[refetchOnMount]
    B -->|Timer| F[refetchInterval]
    C --> G{Data Stale?}
    D --> G
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G -->|Yes| H[Background Refetch]
    G -->|No| I[Return Cached Data]
    H --> J[Update Cache & UI]
data.caption: How React Query decides whether to refetch data based on triggers and staleness.

data.text: You can configure refetch behavior at both the global level (via QueryClient defaults) and per-query level. Global defaults are set once, and individual queries override as needed.

data.title: Configuring refetch triggers per query
data.content: Fine-tune refetch triggers per query based on data criticality and user context.

data.text: Polling keeps data fresh by refetching on a timer. Use it for data that changes frequently and where near-real-time accuracy matters. Combine with `refetchIntervalInBackground: false` to pause polling when the tab is hidden, saving bandwidth.

data.title: Polling a live data feed
data.content: Poll live metrics every 5 seconds while the tab is visible.

data.text: Disabling background refetching reduces server load and prevents disruptive UI updates. Use it for static content, form-heavy pages, or data that updates only on explicit user action.

data.title: Disable refetchOnWindowFocus for Forms
data.text: If a user is filling out a multi-step form, a background refetch on window focus can cause a flash of stale content or lose unsaved input. Set refetchOnWindowFocus: false for form and wizard queries.

data.title: Global override disabling window focus refetch
data.content: Set global default to false, override per query for specific use cases.

data.title: Exercise: Configure Refetching for a Chat App
data.description: A chat application needs fresh messages and a stable user list. Configure refetching for both queries appropriately.
steps: Set refetchInterval: 3000 for the messages query.
Set refetchIntervalInBackground: false to save bandwidth when the tab is hidden.
Set staleTime: 0 for messages since new messages invalidate the cache.
Set staleTime: Infinity for the user list since it rarely changes.
Set refetchOnWindowFocus: true for messages but false for the user list.
data.expectedOutcome: Messages poll every 3 seconds while the tab is visible, the user list loads instantly from cache, and switching tabs does not disrupt either.

items.question: Does background refetching show a loading state?
items.answer: No. Background refetching updates the cache silently. The UI shows the old data until the new data arrives, then re-renders with the fresh data. This is called stale-while-revalidate.

items.question: What is refetchIntervalInBackground?
items.answer: When false (default), polling pauses when the browser tab is hidden. Set it to true only when you need live updates even in background tabs â€” this consumes more battery and bandwidth.

items.question: Will background refetching cause rate limit issues?
items.answer: Yes, if every open tab polls independently. Mitigate with longer intervals, server-side caching, or by disabling polling on inactive tabs.

data.title: Background Refetching Key Points
points: Background refetching keeps data fresh without disrupting the UI.
Window focus and reconnect are the most common and useful triggers.
Use polling with refetchInterval for near-real-time data.
Disable refetching for static or user-input-heavy pages.
data.takeaway: Background refetching is a powerful default, but should be tuned per use case.
